name: status-indicator
purpose: Communicates status, alerts, or progress to the user. Lives at `packages/webkit/src/components/feedback/status-indicator/`.
useWhen: The state of a resource in a table cell, a list row or a detail header: Active, Failed, Paused.
A transitional state such as Deploying or Propagating, with `loading`.
avoidWhen: A count or a very short label attached to another element → use `badge`.
A category or status chip with an optional icon → use `tag`.
A page or section notice with copy and actions → use `message`.
related: badge` — filled count indicator, usually overlaid on an icon or avatar.
tag` — labelled chip for categories and statuses.
spinner` — replaces the dot while `loading` is true.
progress` — continuous progress instead of a discrete state.
bestPractices: Always pass `label`. The default is the literal `'Status'`, and the color alone does not carry the meaning.
Map `severity` to meaning and keep it consistent across the app: `success`, `info`, `warning` and `danger` follow their tokens, `neutral` is muted, and `alt` uses the primary color.
With `loading`, pass the bare verb (`"Deploying"`). The component appends the ellipsis character (`…`, not three periods) and swaps the dot for a spinner.
It is a non-interactive `role="status"` element with no click or keyboard behavior. Don't attach handlers to it.

props.name: severity
props.doc: Severity token driving the status dot color.

props.name: loading
props.doc: Shows loading state and disables activation.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label text. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Status`).

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import StatusIndicator from '@aziontech/webkit/status-indicator'
</script>

<template>
  <StatusIndicator
    severity="success"
    label="Status"
  />
</template>
